subject.title: Several latent session/workspace lifecycle concurrency bugs (native-VNC credential leak, run-status stomp, terminal-hub races)

question: Which of the four findings without a linked fix have enough current-main evidence to remain tracked as confirmed defects, and should the narrow native-auth race be dropped unless a focused reproduction is provided?
rationale: The issue mixes one security-boundary finding with several independently triggered reliability races, and source inspection alone does not establish that every proposed interleaving is reachable or warrants changed behavior.

options.title: Require focused proof per finding
options.body: Keep the umbrella open and accept each remaining fix only with a focused current-main regression test or credible runtime interleaving proof.

options.title: Split confirmed findings now
options.body: Create or request separate canonical issues for the run-status and terminal-hub races, then narrow this umbrella to the native-VNC work.

options.title: Retain all audit candidates
options.body: Keep every source-audit candidate tracked here even without focused reproduction, accepting a broader and less actionable umbrella.

recommendation.title: Require focused proof per finding
recommendation.body: Keep the umbrella open and accept each remaining fix only with a focused current-main regression test or credible runtime interleaving proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history connects this person to the native-VNC endpoint and core interactive-session lifecycle behavior.
